Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Football Amputee World Cup: ‘It’s a must-win game against Iraq’ – Black Challenge coach Source : Benaiah Elorm Dafeamekpor 16 November 2026 5:03pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Ghana’s Black Challenge were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by Colombia in their second Group D match at the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico.
The Black Challenge headed into the encounter needing to bounce back after suffering a disappointing 2-0 defeat to Angola in their opening game but were left frustrated after failing to turn their dominance into victory against Colombia.
Ghana started aggressively, creating several chances in the first half but were repeatedly denied by an impressive display from the Colombian goalkeeper.
Their persistence eventually paid off when star player Mohammed Mubarik produced a brilliant strike to give Ghana the lead.
However, Colombia drew level shortly afterwards, capitalising on their opportunity to restore parity.
Despite Colombia being reduced to six players, the Black Challenge failed to find a winning goal, leaving both sides to share the points.
Head coach Richard Obeng believes Ghana did enough to secure victory but was disappointed that his players could not make their dominance count.
“Today, luck wasn’t on our side. Everybody can see how we played. We played our best. From recovering from the defeat against Angola, we came in much stronger and took possession of the game. But unfortunately for us, it ended in a draw,” he said.
With Ghana’s hopes of progressing to the next stage at stake, Obeng has described their final Group D fixture against Iraq as a must-win encounter.
“We are going back to the drawing board to make sure it’s a must-win game against Iraq. That is what we have to work on. So we are going to work on it tonight before tomorrow,” he added.
The coach says his team will adopt a more attacking approach against Iraq but insists they must remain disciplined defensively.
“We have to attack, but we have to be very vigilant in defending as well. As I watched Angola play Iraq today, it was a game that Iraq also did well. So we have to be vigilant in our attacking, but we are going to come in with more attacking than defending to make sure we can score some goals before the first half,” he said.
Obeng is particularly keen for his players to find the net early, setting a clear target for the team ahead of the decisive encounter.
“We have to score before the first half ends. So that is what we have to work on this evening to make sure we have some wins before the first half ends,” he said.
The Black Challenge will face Iraq on Monday, November 16, knowing that victory is crucial to keeping their hopes of reaching the knockout stage alive.
